question: Why does inquiry continue even after some aspect has been determined?
premises: An already determined aspect can be pushed into the background.
Inquiry then proceeds again and again.
This repeated process takes the form of initial statement, definition, and examination.
inference: Cognitive inquiry is iterative: each determination becomes the background for further questioning and examination.
uncertainties: The exact technical scope of parīkṣaṇa here anticipates later verses.
plain_english: Once a certain aspect has been determined and set in the background, inquiry proceeds again and again through initial statement, definition, and examination.
